_: Name, description and badge live in src/resources/connectors.json so the console and the browser process cannot disagree about them.

notes: Grain publishes no scope parameter - access is whatever the authenticating user has. The empty list is deliberate, not forgotten.
The authorize URL is on grain.com and the token URL is on api.grain.com. They are different hosts; sending either to the other fails.

PKCE with S256 is supported and is what Flux uses: code_challenge is a random string, SHA-256 hashed and base64url encoded. A desktop client has nowhere to keep client_secret, and Grain marks the secret required only for server-side applications.
The token request is JSON, not form-encoded - Grain's own examples POST Content-Type: application/json.
Access tokens carry expires_in (3600 in Grain's examples) and a rotating refresh_token. Persist the new refresh token on every exchange.
Some legacy clients get neither refresh_token nor expires_in, in which case the access token does not expire. Do not assume the refresh fields are present.

personal_token.label: Personal Access Token
notes: Grain publishes no fixed prefix; the field is empty deliberately.
Scoped to the generating user - the same access that user has in Grain, nothing more. This is the tier Flux should offer.

workspace_token.label: Workspace Access Token
notes: Reaches ALL DATA in the workspace, in Grain's own words - every recording of every member, not only the holder's. Do not offer this by default; a meeting-notes task never needs the whole company's calls.
It also changes behaviour: the attendance filter and the private_notes include are Personal API only and simply do not apply, while the upload endpoint requires an explicit user_id to own the result.
Public-Api-Version is mandatory on every call, not optional. 2025-10-31 is the current version; it gates which fields exist, so pin it and change it deliberately.
v1 (the API Beta) is being sunset and some features are not carried over. Nothing here uses it.
Several reads are POSTs - list recordings, get recording, list users, list teams and list meeting types all take POST with a JSON body. That is Grain's design, not a typo.
Pagination is a cursor: the response's cursor field is passed back as a param, and is null on the last page.

get_transcript.label: Get a transcript
get_transcript.notes: JSON array of { start, end, speaker, participant_id, text }, timestamps in ms from the start of the recording. Add .txt, .vtt or .srt to the path for the text forms; .txt is 'Speaker: line' and is the cheapest thing to hand a model.

list_teams.label: List teams
list_teams.notes: Needed to resolve the team id for the recording filter.

list_meeting_types.label: List meeting types
list_meeting_types.notes: Needed to resolve the meeting_type id for the recording filter. Each carries an internal/external scope.

filters._: The recording filter object, passed to list_recordings.
filters.caution: Grain's own table describes these two backwards - it says before_datetime returns recordings whose start_datetime is AFTER the date, and after_datetime returns those BEFORE it. The names and the prose disagree. Treat the names as correct, but check the first response's dates before trusting a date-bounded sync; getting this wrong silently returns the wrong half of the history.
filters.participant_scope: internal | external - team meetings versus customer meetings.

includes._: The recording include object. Everything is off by default, so a bare list returns metadata only - ask for what the task needs and no more.
includes.ai_summary: Markdown text of the AI summary. The usual thing a task actually wants.
includes.ai_action_items: Action items with status, observed timestamp, text and an optional assignee.
includes.ai_template_sections: Object, not a boolean: { format: json|markdown|text, allowed_sections: [...] }. allowed_sections filters by section title, case insensitively.
includes.participants: Includes scope (internal/external/unknown), confirmed_attendee and observed join/leave times. Grain notes those times are what its recorder saw, not ground truth.
includes.calendar_event: ical_uid and the scheduled start/end, which is what to join on against a calendar connector.
includes.screenshares: Screenshare ranges in ms with the sharing participant.
includes.private_notes: The user's own notes. Personal API only.
includes.hubspot: HubSpot company and deal ids, and hs_contact_id on participants.

headers.Retry-After: Seconds to wait. Only present on a 429.

rate_limits.note: Grain returns the budget on every response, so a client can pace itself rather than discovering the limit by hitting it. Read x-ratelimit-remaining and slow down before it reaches zero.

webhooks.note: Grain calls them hooks. Flux has no public endpoint to register, so it polls; recorded so the alternative is not re-derived.
webhooks.reachability_test: Grain calls the URL on creation and refuses to create the hook unless it answers 2xx.
webhooks.signature: None documented. Grain publishes no signing secret or signature header for hooks, so a receiver cannot verify a delivery came from Grain and must treat the payload as a hint to go and fetch, never as trusted data.

never_expose: PUT and DELETE on /tags, /users and /teams - these change who can see a recording. Sharing is a permissions decision, not a data edit, and nothing in the Flux catalogue needs it.
The upload endpoints - they put media into someone's workspace.

notes: Every host, path, header, filter, include, hook type and rate limit above is taken verbatim from Grain's own v2 API document, which the user supplied in full.

The only ref is the token page the document itself names, because the document was pasted rather than fetched and its canonical URL was not captured. The content is first-hand; the citation is thin. Add the real docs link when it is next to hand rather than inventing one.
The before_datetime / after_datetime contradiction under `filters.caution` is Grain's, not a transcription error. It is recorded rather than silently resolved.
